title: journal-batched-atomicity: Use JournalWriteBatch for cross-event atomicity (true group commit)
description: Feature P2-14. Master §61 Fjall Storage Contract defines the durability model; today, journaled events are written one at a time even when many events are ready. JournalWriteBatch (batch.rs:46-62) supports cross-keyspace atomicity. The runtime journals never use it. StorageRuntimeJournal::append_sequenced (shard/lifecycle/chunk_002.rs:294-315) constructs per-event Fjall batches. QueuedStorageRuntimeJournal::flush_batch (queue/writer.rs:144-150,169-176) calls append_queued_indexed_unpersisted per item in a loop. The result: 1000 events produce 1000 Fjall commits, not 1. This bead has 4 sub-phases: (14a) extend RuntimeJournal::append_sequenced to accept &[RuntimeJournalEvent] and use JournalWriteBatch::commit per call; (14b) add coalesce_window_us: u64 to ShardConfig (default 100µs) and a coalescing layer in Shard::tick that batches commands within the window; (14c) feature-flag batched_atomicity = false default; flip to true after A/B benchmark shows ≥3× throughput; (14d) update master §61 from 'Atomic Cross-Keyspace Writes' to 'Atomic Cross-Keyspace Batched Writes (per coalesce window)'.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL batch journal events within a coalesce window into a single Fjall commit
THE SYSTEM SHALL use JournalWriteBatch for cross-keyspace atomicity when batched_atomicity is enabled

event_driven.trigger: WHEN Shard::tick processes 100 commands within a 100µs window and batched_atomicity is true
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL emit a single Fjall commit containing all 100 commands' journal events

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user passes --batched-atomicity on `vb ipc-serve`
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL set the feature flag at runtime; default is false

unwanted.condition: IF the coalesce window is set to 0
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT default to 'no batching' silently; it must return InvalidCoalesceWindow
unwanted.because: Operators must explicitly opt in to the no-batching path for benchmarking

unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT partially apply the batch; it must roll back and return a typed BatchCommitFailed
unwanted.because: Master §61: 'Atomic Cross-Keyspace Writes' — partial application violates the contract

preconditions: batched_atomicity feature is enabled in ShardConfig (or via --batched-atomicity flag)
Coalesce window is a positive u64 (default 100µs)
postconditions: N events within the window produce 1 Fjall commit, not N
On commit failure, no events are partially applied (atomicity preserved)
invariants: Per-event durability: each event is either fully persisted or not at all
Sequence numbers remain monotonic per run (master §68.5)

happy: batched_atomicity_1000_events_produces_1_fjall_commit: with batched_atomicity = true and coalesce_window_us = 100, 1000 events in a workload produce exactly 1 Fjall commit (instrumented counter)
batched_atomicity_disabled_reverts_to_per_event_commits: with batched_atomicity = false, 1000 events produce 1000 commits (no regression)
batched_atomicity_ab_benchmark_shows_3x_throughput: the A/B benchmark (batched_atomicity on/off, same workload) shows ≥3× throughput on the batched path
error: batched_atomicity_with_commit_failure_rolls_back: a Fjall commit failure rolls back the entire batch, no partial events
edge: batched_atomicity_with_empty_batch_skips_commit: a tick with 0 commands produces 0 Fjall commits (no spurious commit)

files: crates/vb_runtime/src/shard/tick.rs (Shard::tick; where the coalescing layer goes)
patterns: Pattern: existing Fjall write batch primitives in vb_storage (JournalWriteBatch::commit, WriteBatch::commit)
Pattern: existing feature flags in ShardConfig (e.g., batched_writes is partial; this bead completes it)
questions: What is the default coalesce window? (Spec: 100µs, configurable.)
Should the A/B benchmark be a separate bead or part of this one? (Spec: part of this one, with evidence.)

security_failures.failure: An attacker exploits the batch to hide a malicious event among many benign events, batching a side-effect with no journal entry
security_failures.prevention: Each event in the batch is journaled in order; the journal entry is created before the side effect (master §68.1)

usability_failures.failure: Operator can't tell whether batched_atomicity is enabled at runtime
usability_failures.prevention: vb status shows the active coalesce_window_us and batched_atomicity flag

data_integrity_failures.failure: Batch commit succeeds but a single event in the batch is corrupted on disk
data_integrity_failures.prevention: BLAKE3 + CRC32C envelope on every record; corrupt records are detected on read

integration_failures.failure: The A/B benchmark shows no improvement, leaving the operator wondering if the feature is broken
integration_failures.prevention: Run the A/B benchmark as part of this bead's evidence; commit the numbers

phase_1: Write test test_batched_atomicity_1000_events_produces_1_fjall_commit (instrumented counter on Fjall commits)
Run the A/B benchmark and record the result in .evidence/batched_atomicity_ab.json
phase_2: Phase 14a: Extend RuntimeJournal::append_sequenced to accept &[RuntimeJournalEvent] and use JournalWriteBatch::commit per call
Phase 14b: Add coalesce_window_us: u64 to ShardConfig (default 100µs); add a coalescing layer in Shard::tick that batches commands within the window
Phase 14c: Add batched_atomicity feature flag (default false); plumb it through ShardConfig and cmd_ipc_serve
phase_3: Phase 14d: Update master §61 from 'Atomic Cross-Keyspace Writes' to 'Atomic Cross-Keyspace Batched Writes (per coalesce window)'
phase_4: Run `moon run :test -p vb_runtime -p vb_storage` and verify all new tests pass
Run the A/B benchmark with batched_atomicity on and off; assert ≥3× throughput improvement

similar_implementations: AWS Step Functions journal batching; same model
external_references: Master §68.5 Journal sequence numbers are monotonic per run

apis_that_do_not_exist: RuntimeJournal::append_sequenced(&[RuntimeJournalEvent]) does not exist; this bead adds the slice variant
no_placeholder_values: Do NOT use coalesce_window_us = 0 as a default; it must be 100µs minimum
